1-1.text: Part one. Reading coordinates. ... A coordinate grid has two number lines. The x axis goes across. The y axis goes up. They meet at the origin, nought, nought.

1-2.text: To find the point 2, 3, start at the origin. Go along 2 first, then up 3. Along the corridor, then up the stairs!

1-3.text: The order matters. 3, 2 means 3 along and 2 up. That is a different point!

2-1.text: Part two. Four quadrants. ... The axes keep going past zero. To the left of the origin, x is negative. Below the origin, y is negative.

2-2.text: P is 3 to the left and 2 up, so P is at negative 3, 2.

2-3.text: Q is 2 to the right and 3 down, so Q is at 2, negative 3. Still x first, then y.

3-1.text: Part three. Midpoints and shapes. ... The midpoint is exactly halfway between two points. Here are A, at 2, 4, and B, at 8, 10.

3-2.text: Find halfway for x, then halfway for y. Halfway between 2 and 8 is 5. Halfway between 4 and 10 is 7. So the midpoint is 5, 7.

3-3.text: A quick way: add and halve. 2 plus 8, divided by 2, is 5. And 4 plus 10, divided by 2, is 7.

3-4.text: Grids help with shapes too. A square has corners at 1, 1, at 4, 1, and at 4, 4. The missing corner is 1, 4.

4-1.text: Part four. Straight-line graphs. ... A rule like y equals x plus 1 makes a straight line. Make a table: when x is 0, 1, 2, 3, y is 1, 2, 3, 4.

4-2.text: Plot the points nought, 1. Then 1, 2. Then 2, 3. And 3, 4. They line up, so join them with a ruler.

4-3.text: y equals 2 x plus 1 is steeper: y goes up 2 for every 1 across. In y equals m x plus c, m is the gradient, which means how steep, and c is where the line crosses the y axis.

4-4.text: Some lines are special. y equals 4 is flat, or horizontal: every point on it has y equal to 4. x equals 2 goes straight up, or vertical.

5-1.text: Part five. Real-life graphs. ... Graphs show real life too. A tank holds 60 litres of water. It drains at 5 litres every minute.

5-2.text: After 8 minutes, 5 times 8 is 40 litres drained, so 60 minus 40 is 20 litres left. You can read it from the graph: up from 8, then across.

5-3.text: The tank is empty when the line reaches the time axis: after 60 divided by 5, which is 12 minutes.
